newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: East Europe stock markets surge but slowdown seen.
newsitem.headline: East Europe stock markets surge but slowdown seen.

text.p: Most east European stock markets were in bullish mood this week but dealers were pessimistic about strong growth prospects in the short and medium term.

Warsaw, Prague, and Bucharest posted year-highs while Slovenia's SBI index stunned investors by hitting an all-time high on Monday and then plunging by more than one fifth over the next three sessions.
The CESI Central European Share Index fell by 0.87 percent on the week to 1,705.48.
WARSAW
The WIG index hit a 34-month high on Thursday but analysts said this week's slower growth, including a downward correction on Tuesday, suggested the market would extend gains more gradually.

"It seems the change in mood (this week) had a healing effect on what started two weeks ago and now there's a chance for more gradual growth in the near term," said Roman Sosnowski, an analyst at Bank Staropolski brokerage.
The main market has risen 10.7 percent in February, apparently fuelled by foreign buying.

Analysts said the market was probably strong enough to keep rising despite a Finance Ministry decision on Thursday to free up fuel prices. The move could add up to one percent to the government's 1997 year-on-year inflation target of 13 percent.
PRAGUE
The PX50 posted a two-year high of 603.0 at mid-week but slipped back slightly on Thursday on fears that major issues may have risen too high, too fast.
In the week to Thursday, the PX50 was virtually unchanged from Monday's open, edging up 0.3 percent to 601.4.

Despite continued strength in blue chips, dealers warned that recent gains had been made on generally low volumes. In the absence of new information on company fundamentals they were sceptical about the shares' short-term prospects.
"I would expect that the prices of the blue chips are going to go down during the next week but probably not by much," said Ivan Kusacek of Zivnostenska Banka.
BUDAPEST
The BUX remained practically unchanged through the week but a less than half percentage point drop on the index concealed some volatile price movements.
On Thursday, the BUX index closed at 5,635.99 points, down 21.34 points from last Friday.

Traders said a four-day long corrective period ended on Wednesday, leaving room for small rises before the release of corporate results. By Thursday, 16 of the bourse's 44 companies had published their figures before the February 15 deadline.
LJUBLJANA
The Slovenian SBI index slumped after hitting an all-time high on Monday of 1,655.4. By Thursday the index was 22 percent below Monday's opening level.

Traders said the fall was caused by a central bank decree forcing foreign portfolio investors to trade through special custody or fiduciary accounts opened at any of Slovenia's 14 fully-licensed banks.
BRATISLAVA
The SAX index on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) continued to grow this week, boosted mainly by strong foreign demand. The 16-share index rose 4.97 points to close at 194.8 on Thursday.

"We think that the current strong demand from foreign investors should keep the market running up for some time, and that the SAX can even break the 200-point level in the foreseeable future," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.
BUCHAREST
With major issue Azomures absent from the Bucharest Stock Exchange, buying interest focused on other stocks, sending most prices higher and pushing its two unofficial indices to year highs.

Turnover climbed to an all-time high of 6.3 billion lei early in the week on heavy trading in fertiliser maker Azomures, but sagged on Thursday to 112 million with the stock suspended after a share split.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks posted losses this week in what analysts saw as a market reaction to tighter controls on foreign investment imposed by neighbouring Slovenia.
But the recovery that drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka were making in London was expected to stabilise Zagreb prices.
Pliva was Thursday's most active issue with 4,511 shares sold, closing at 457 kuna, five up from last Friday. Its GDRs traded at $16.75 in London.
Zagrebacka lost 36 kuna from last week, ending at 1,800 kuna. Its GDRs traded higher at $30.625 on Seaq International.
